checks.reason: PhysicalKSBoxFactorialData expands literally to one FactorialRawJetFamily F with F(0,0)=f, a finite common squared L2 budget for all derivatives of any fixed finite total order on the half-width 1/128 box, and all Y/T successor weak identities on that same box. ProductLocalWeakDirectional includes local L2 membership of both functions and the compact smooth-test integral identity for the displayed direction. The existential F occurs before every derivative index and profile order, so the conclusion is one coherent family for each chart/solution/center/scale instance, not unrelated families selected anew for each order.
checks.limit: F may depend on the chart and displayed physical data. The theorem does not supply one global derivative family simultaneously across different centers or charts, and does not identify F with pointwise classical derivatives.

checks.reason: On the smaller half-width 1/256 box, the output separately asserts FactorialLocalMemLp and the profile bound for every r. The profile is a finite maximum over base multiindices of sums of actual restricted eLpNorm(...,2).toReal values of y-monomial-weighted shifted fields of the same F. FactorialLocalMemLp explicitly proves every underlying field is MemLp 2, excluding a vacuous small value caused by toReal of infinity. The base derivative cost is |alpha|+|beta|+min(|alpha|,4). The outer indices (eta,theta,gamma) satisfy |eta|+|theta|<=2, |gamma|<=2 and |eta|+2|theta|<=|gamma|+2; their fields are y^gamma smul F(alpha+eta,beta+theta).
checks.limit: The displayed result bounds this weighted local L2 profile. It is not yet a pointwise derivative estimate, classical smooth/analytic representative, or KS descent theorem.

checks.reason: For fixed external real Z,E, the theorem chooses C_H,M,A with lower bounds one before f, its graph premise, g and its representative premises, L,R,epsilon and their admissibility conditions, both nuclear chart indices and every unit center, and the pair branch. C_H is taken from the existing all-chart physical H12 theorem; M,A come from the existing all-chart coefficient/source theorem. The body reuses exactly those witnesses. Source size F0=M*norm(g(0))*sqrt(V) and input squared H12 budget W=(L^2+norm(g(0))^2)*C_H retain only their explicitly allowed dependence on representative and Lipschitz data.
checks.allowed_dependence: C_H,M,A and the derived common profile constant may depend on Z,E. The theorem does not claim independence from Z,E.

checks.reason: The input is scalarHamiltonianGraph 2 Z f ((E:Complex) smul f), with f in the actual six-dimensional complex SpatialL2 quotient. That graph explicitly provides L2 first and second weak partial derivatives and the almost-everywhere relation h=-(1/2) sum of diagonal second derivatives + CoulombPotential*f. The separate physical representative g is continuous and equal to f almost everywhere for actual configuration volume; it is not an arbitrary unrelated function. g, its continuity and the same AE equality are passed unchanged into the physical equation and H12 theorems. In particular the proof does not directly pull an arbitrary AE equality through the nonlinear KS map or evaluate an Lp quotient at the origin.
checks.limit: The theorem is conditional on this defined scalar graph and the supplied continuous representative. It does not construct that representative or independently identify the graph with another self-adjoint realization.

checks.reason: The actual solution used throughout is epsilon^{-1} smul (g(epsilon smul x)-g(0)), composed first with the unchanged nonlinear nuclear/pair KS lift and then with inverse spectator reindexing. Positive epsilon guarantees its normalization is meaningful. epsilon<=min(1,R/4) supplies both epsilon<=1 for coefficient estimates and epsilon<=R/4 for the H12 theorem. Together with epsilon>0 it also implies R>0, so the absence of a separate R>0 premise is harmless. The source has no inverse epsilon: subtracting the constant g(0) from the homogeneous equation with coefficient epsilon*b and dividing by epsilon gives -b smul g(0), exactly as the physical equation theorem states.
checks.limit: Local Lipschitz behavior on the physical ball is an explicit input. No derivative at the origin or limit as epsilon tends to zero is asserted.

checks.reason: The existing H12 branch uses the same physical L,R,epsilon conditions. Its initial amplitude estimate comes from the true Configuration norm of the KS images, which is <2 on the fixed annulus. With epsilon<=R/4, the scaled physical image lies strictly inside ball(0,R), allowing the local Lipschitz estimate and uniform norm bound 2L for the normalized difference. Compact restricted L2 budgets follow using actual product volume. The H12 common theorem then uses a finite sum of nonnegative chart budgets plus one, chosen before all physical solutions and centers. W is nonnegative because C_H>=1 and L^2+norm(g(0))^2>=0.
checks.limit: This review checks the physical amplitude/radius input and common-budget assembly. It does not independently redo the whole finite H12 iteration or all its analytic estimates.

checks.reason: For each canonical unit t0, the nuclear branch supplies the physical center (twoElectronSpectatorPositionEquiv i).symm(t0), whose norm is exactly one. Applying the forward equivalence recovers t0, so the H12 region is precisely the reindex preimage of the canonical half-width 1/128 box. The pair branch does the same with pairCenterEquiv.symm; its index-zero reindexing agrees with physicalSpectatorReindexAt(0). The weak coordinate transport maps each full word through the inverse coordinate equivalence, preserves list length and every squared budget, transports the weak test identity with actual product-volume preservation, and then converts words to mixed multiindices on the open box. The resulting function and W are exactly those used in the target.
checks.limit: The transport is a linear reindexing of the seven-dimensional KS coordinates, not a nonlinear KS change of physical measure.

checks.reason: For each branch, scalar_coulomb_*_physical_box_equation supplies smoothness of the actual pulled-back coefficient B and source, local L2 of the exact normalized physical function, and the original compact-test weak equation on the half-width 1/64 box, including both test integrabilities. Its equation component is extracted without altering the integrands. The coefficient/source budget theorem is specialized at amplitude g(0), so its B and src match those equation inputs literally. The source is nuclearKSPotential(i,Z,epsilon*E) or pairKSPotential(Z,epsilon*E), multiplied by -g(0); the coefficient additionally has the leading epsilon. Neither a differentiated equation nor a source bound for an unrelated function is an input.
checks.limit: The global off-collision regularity and KS removability chain used by the imported physical equation theorem was inspected at its consumed interface, not re-proved in full.

checks.reason: The common local theorem requires B/src smooth and f locally L2 with the original equation on the 1/64 box, coefficient and full source-word bounds plus genuine H12 on the 1/128 box, and nonnegative M,F0 with A>=1. Every item is supplied by the corresponding physical theorem with the same t0 and functions. The chosen F0 is nonnegative by M>=1, norm nonnegativity and sqrt nonnegativity. Its source squared budget is exactly (F0*A^n*n!)^2; W is the actual squared H12 budget. The conclusion of that theorem is definitionally PhysicalKSBoxFactorialData, including all four family/weak-chain fields and the exact profile expression. No all-order solution family, factorial solution estimate or recurrence is assumed in the new coupling.
checks.limit: The generic local factorial theorem and its analytic recurrence are inherited dependencies; this is a premise/target matching review of their physical instantiation.

checks.reason: The nuclear equation and local theorem use c=4; the pair equation and local theorem use c=1 with the unscaled physical center convention. The alternatives c=1 or c=4 are proved by rfl in the respective branches. commonKSBoxFactorialConstant(M) is the maximum of the fixed-box constants at c=1 and c=4. The generic comparison increases only nonnegative factors and powers, yielding the identical common constant for all three charts. At bY=1/128 and gap=1/256, the raw factors simplify to 498*sqrt(W), prefactor 12*C*A and exponential base 3072*C*A, exactly as stated.

The target module explicitly sets autoImplicit false. PhysicalKSBoxFactorialData has exactly its displayed parameters; no section variable introduces a hidden regularity premise. The final theorem has only the displayed original graph, continuous AE representative, local Lipschitz, positive-scale and unit-center conditions after choosing constants. All higher weak derivative data and profile bounds occur in its conclusion. Existing compiler-PASS receipt matches the entire current source byte-for-byte.
